summary: WAF header rewrite evicts tenant model pin, triggering silent fallback during canary window
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (BrightForms) reported that during a scheduled canary rollout for redwood/open-7b-v2 the tenant's traffic sporadically received responses from the fallback model (redwood/open-7b-v1-backup) even though the tenant had an active model pin. Symptoms appeared only for a subset of requests proxied through the customer's third-party WAF (FastShield) which rewrites/normalizes inbound headers.

Impact:
- Intermittent incorrect model responses for BrightForms production workload serving user-facing recommendations.
- Occurred during canary window (weighting 10% -> 30%), customer observed degraded output quality for ~7% of requests for ~45 minutes.
- Business impact: potential incorrect recommendations surfaced to end-users; customer classified as enterprise and flagged for incident handling.

Environment:
- Region: prod-us-east
- Ingress path: CDN -> FastShield WAF -> Redwood edge-proxy -> api-gateway -> routing layer -> serving-runtime
- Tenant pin: brightforms-prod pinned to redwood/open-7b-v2 on control-plane

Steps to reproduce (as observed):
1) Send authenticated request with tenant session token and x-tenant-version header set (used for pinning) through FastShield WAF.
2) WAF rewrites Authorization header to canonical form and strips x-tenant-version for certain request patterns (POSTs with a multipart form).
3) Edge-proxy receives request without x-tenant-version; routing falls back to cached cookie-based affinity which had an expired lease for ~10% of sessions and routes to default variant.
4) Serving-runtime returns responses from fallback model for those requests.

Logs / Observations:
- Edge-proxy logs show repeated 302->router handoffs where header x-tenant-version is absent for affected requests.
- api-gateway trace: request_id=7f8b3a shows header mutation between FastShield and our edge.
- Routing debug snapshot (2026-03-01T14:12Z): affinity_lease_miss_count spike correlated with canary weight change.
- No 5xx errors; requests succeeded but were routed to unintended variant.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis: Header mutation by WAF caused control-plane pin lookup path (which prefers explicit header) to skip, and in combination with an expiring affinity lease on the edge, routing selected fallback variant silently.
- Reproduced internally by replaying requests through a staging FastShield instance with header rewrite rules enabled; behavior matched production.
- Verified that when x-tenant-version is present downstream of WAF, pin is honored consistently.
- Routing logic currently considers header > cookie > token; when header missing and cookie lease expired, routing performs best-effort selection which can pick fallback model if canary weight calculation and cache state align unfavorably.
- Related: found a small time-window race during canary weight transitions where lease-renewal requests are batched and may be delayed by up to 2s under load.

Workaround (customer-facing):
- Short term: Instruct BrightForms to disable the FastShield rule that strips x-tenant-version for POSTs (they accepted and pushed change at 2026-03-01T15:00Z).
- Platform-side: Applied a temporary edge-proxy rule to prefer parsing x-tenant-version from the query param if header absent (mitigated within 30 minutes).

Proposed fix / next steps:
1) Routing change: Add a robust header fallback chain that extracts tenant-version from multiple safe locations (headers, cookies, signed token) before falling back to affinity; add logging where explicit pin is absent. (PR drafted: routing#8123).
2) Improve edge lease behavior: reduce lease expiry jitter during canary weight changes and make lease-renewal non-blocking under bursts.
3) Instrumentation: Emit an observability metric whenever routing resolves without explicit pin and routes to non-pinned variant during a rollout.
4) Security review: Confirm that extracting x-tenant-version from query param is safe for enterprise tenants; avoid exposing secrets in URLs.

Resolution notes (work-in-progress):
- Customer applied WAF rule change; immediate regression stopped.
- Edge temporary rule applied to prefer query param; mitigated while routing PR is reviewed.
- Routing PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/8123) under code review and QA.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- ENG-ops to complete routing PR and run canary test harness (owner: Maya Chen, ETA: 2026-03-10).
- SRE to add metric and alert for "pin_resolution_fallback" during rollouts (owner: Diego Ramirez, ETA: 2026-03-08).
- CS to update enterprise onboarding doc recommending tenants avoid header-stripping WAF rules or to use supported token-based pinning methods (owner: Priya Singh, ETA: 2026-03-12).

References:
- Slack thread: #support-brightforms (link: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C12345/p1677623456000123)
- Reproduction replay: gs://redwood-replays/brightforms/2026-03-01/fastshield-replay.tar.gz
